target_customer: Fashion and apparel brands and retailers using 3D garment simulation for design and virtual try-on
problem: Online shoppers doubt how clothes will fit and brands lack cheap accurate 3D garment content. Avametric simulated cloth on customizable body avatars.
business_model: B2B software licensing (SaaS for digital garments and e-commerce try-on)

founders.name: David (Dave) Jackson
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

founders.name: James O'Brien
founders.background_notes: Described by VentureBeat as an Academy Award-winning digital animator and computer scientist. Not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Ari Bloom
founders.background_notes: Named CEO by VentureBeat in 2016 and by Textile World in 2018; not a founder per sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate physics-based cloth simulation on body avatars took four years of development with an Academy Award-winning animation scientist, close to research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: The simulation engine was hard to replicate and Gerber later wanted it for its own 3D workflow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gerber integrated Avametric's engine into AccuMark 3D starting November 2017 and acquired the company in October 2018 rather than copying it.

market_need_then: Fit uncertainty drives online apparel returns and shoppers visit stores to check fit; Gerber's survey in 2018 found over 60% of fashion companies planned 3D adoption within three years. Demand evidence from 2014 itself was not found.

branding.community_and_virality: TrendHunter covered it as an augmented reality fitting room app, undated.

brand_strength.rationale: Only trademark filings from February 2016 and a trade-blog mention were found; the AVAMETRIC mark is listed as dead.

outcome_analysis: Avametric spent about four years building accurate cloth simulation, raised $10.5M led by Khosla Ventures in March 2016, and became a technology supplier to Gerber before Gerber acquired it in October 2018 on undisclosed terms. The exit looks like a technology acquisition for a hard-to-copy engine rather than a venture-scale consumer outcome.
notes: The company website returned 503 during the check. The 2016 round is labelled other because VentureBeat gives no series; other outlets call it Series A or B. An earlier Khosla-led seed with YC participation is mentioned in a press release summary but no amount was found. The press release at businesswire returned 403. No competitor sources dated near 2014 were found; later lists (Metail etc.) are not as of founding. Michael Bloom style details not applicable.
